## Gates

`just check` composes `just check-hygiene`: ops-check, `ops-docs check` and `tasks check`.
`just ci-check-hygiene` runs the portable hygiene checks (`ops-check` and `ops-docs check`);
`tasks check` requires the private detached records repository and stays on the mandatory
local path in `check-hygiene` and the git hooks.
The pre-commit hook runs the same hygiene. The suite is pytest under `python/`: `just setup`
once per worktree (frozen `uv sync`), then `just test-one <path | path::test | -k expr>`
on affected tests while working and again before committing; the hooks run the
hygiene. Tests marked `bwrap` need bubblewrap and unprivileged user namespaces. Tests
marked `pi` also need the pinned pi 1.1.0 install (`PI_DIR`, default
`~/.local/share/pi/1.1.0`) and node (`NODE_DIR` when `/usr/bin/node` would shadow
`rg` or `fd`), and `python/tests/test_analyst_check.py` is run locally when touching
the analyst launch or toolchain because the hosted workflow has neither pi nor node.
On a fresh clone, `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`.

Test execution policy is `.tt.toml` at this checkout's Git top level (each worktree
reads its own), never task records or a sibling checkout; tt alone reads it. `test` and
`test-fast` are the broad targets it can skip; `test-one` and `check-hygiene` always run.
Local broad suites are off (`automatic_broad = false`): `just test` and `just test-fast`
record a skip, the hosted workflow below runs the full suite on every branch push, and
`just test-full` runs it here when you need it. Rollback sets `automatic_broad = true`,
restores `just test-fast` (pytest-testmon) before each commit in the paragraph above,
updates `test_the_repository_policy_disables_only_the_broad_suites` to match, and records
`policy: enabled at <RFC3339-UTC> revision <full-sha>` on the adoption task autonomy-23aeff
(tt-policy:autonomy) at the landed rollback.
`just test-full` (or `TT_FORCE=1 just test`) runs the full suite deliberately and returns
its status. testmon reselects only on Python changes, so a justfile or hook edit runs
`just test-one tests/test_front_door.py`. The hooks time mandatory hygiene alone and call
the suites as separate requests: hook durations from this change on are incomparable
with earlier whole-hook durations.

Remote coverage: `.github/workflows/test.yml` runs setup, a namespace and TLS egress proof,
`ci-check-hygiene` and the forced full suite on every branch push (and manual dispatch) to
origin; tags and pull-request events run nothing. The job lifts Ubuntu's AppArmor
restriction on unprivileged user namespaces with a runtime sysctl on its disposable VM,
an approved exception that is never persisted and never applies to a host. `ci_suite_refs`
declares that schedule so a covered push takes the shorter hook; the declaration is intent,
not proof that the pushed head passed. The hosted hygiene has known gaps: `tasks check`
requires the private detached records repository, and ops-check cannot compare
vendored tools with an ops checkout it lacks, so both stay mandatory locally. The paid live-egress
recipe runs in neither place.

## Layout

- `docs/` — typed current reference and guide documents ([docs/envelope.md](docs/envelope.md), [docs/egress.md](docs/egress.md), [docs/records.md](docs/records.md), [docs/development.md](docs/development.md)).
- Task records, design specs, implementation plans, briefs, and handoffs live in
  the project's records directory, committed in the records repository, never in this
  tree.
- `python/` — the `verifiably-autonomy` package (`python/src/autonomy/`), its tests (`python/tests/`), and `python/scripts/egress_live.py`.
- `tools/` — `tt`, `ops-check`, `ops-docs` vendored from ops; `family.toml` published
  from verifiably/docs.
- `.github/workflows/` — hosted verification workflow (`.github/workflows/test.yml`).

## Rules

- No kernel import: `autonomy` reaches `beliefs` only through `science`'s commands as
  tools and published record formats; a private kernel path would let the envelope bypass
  the surface it constrains.
- Authority order: `identity.toml` names `docs/envelope.md`, `docs/egress.md`, and
  `docs/records.md` as this repository's reference authority; update the corresponding
  `docs/*.md` document in the same commit as any behavior, protocol, or schema change.
- Cross-repository citations to verifiably/beliefs or verifiably/docs use GitHub URLs,
  never relative paths into sibling checkouts, which break on GitHub.
